plain: That cannot decay or be made corrupt; of a person, cannot be bribed.

webster.text: That cannot corrupt or decay; not admitting of corruption.

more.text: That cannot be bribed; inflexibly just and upright.

example.quote: A man might go to the Senate with an incorruptible integrity, arid the strongest attachment to the interest of his state.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, New York Convention, June 23, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
